user.title: Astro Planner
user.description: Every AstroWeather site is selected; untick any you don't want. Coordinates are read from AstroWeather, and each site's Bortle class is estimated from nearby towns (AstroWeather doesn't provide it).

data.review_sites: Review each site's details (name, Bortle class, drive time, coordinates)

site.title: Site: {site}
site.description: Coordinates are read from AstroWeather and the Bortle class is estimated from nearby towns; fill in a field only to override it. Bortle 1 is the darkest sky.

data.name: Name (optional)
data.drive_minutes: Drive time in minutes (optional; if empty it is looked up after setup)

abort.single_instance_allowed: Astro Planner is already set up.

menu_options.targets: Targets: altitude, brightness, field of view, watch list
menu_options.edit_sites: Edit all sites as a list

data.review_sites: Review each site's details (name, Bortle class, drive time, coordinates)

data.name: Name (optional)
data.drive_minutes: Drive time in minutes (optional; if empty it is looked up after setup)

data.min_gc_altitude: Minimum core altitude for site scores
data.max_moon_illumination: Max moon illumination while the moon is up
data.calendar_min_altitude: Calendar: core counts above this altitude
data.calendar_best_minutes: Calendar: a full-length (pink) night has a core window of at least
data.good_score_threshold: Score at which a night counts as good (alert events)
data.auto_drive_time: Look up drive times from your Home Assistant location

menu_options.edit_domes: Edit the list and glow settings

find_domes.title: Find nearby cities
find_domes.description: Looks up populated places around your Home Assistant location and your sites using GeoNames (CC BY 4.0), falling back to Wikidata. Nearby towns are combined into metro areas. This downloads a ~11 MB file once and caches it for 30 days.

review_domes.title: Review light domes
review_domes.description: Found {found} cities within {radius} km via {source} ({considered} places considered). Your existing entries are kept. Edit or remove anything, then save.

edit_domes.title: Light domes
edit_domes.description: Cities whose glow can affect the core, each with name, latitude, longitude and population.

data.dome_sigma: Angular spread of a city's glow
data.dome_warning_threshold: Penalty at which a dome warning shows

targets.title: Targets
targets.description: Controls which Messier objects, planets and custom targets are ranked. The field of view is the smaller side of your camera and scope's view; leave it at 0 to show everything. Watched targets (the Milky Way core included) fire their own good-night events.

custom_targets.title: Custom targets
custom_targets.description: Extra objects to plan, each with a name, ra (hours as 5.59 or 05:35:17) and dec (degrees as 22.01 or +22:00:52), and optionally magnitude and size (arcminutes).

edit_sites.title: Edit sites
edit_sites.description: One entry per site: `entity` (an AstroWeather weather entity) plus optional `name`, `bortle` (1-9), `drive_minutes`, and `latitude` and `longitude` together. Leave out anything you want read from AstroWeather or estimated. Handy for backing up or restoring your sites.

error.invalid_domes: Each light dome needs a name, latitude and longitude.
error.invalid_targets: Each custom target needs a name, a valid ra (0-24 hours) and a valid dec (-90 to 90 degrees).
error.invalid_sites: Each site needs a weather.* entity; Bortle must be 1-9, latitude and longitude must be given together and be valid numbers.

progress.lookup: Looking up nearby cities. The first lookup downloads the GeoNames file, which can take a minute.

abort.lookup_failed: Couldn't reach any city data service: {errors}. Try again later, or add cities by hand under 'Edit the list'.

state.target_good: Watched target forecast to be good
state.target_dropped: Watched target no longer looks good

options.any: Any night (rank by sky quality, Milky Way or not)

best_night.name: Best night
best_night.description: Finds the best upcoming nights, ranking your sites by sky quality and the weather forecast, with the Milky Way core lifting a night's score when it's up. Returns the result as response data.

days.name: Days to search
days.description: How many nights ahead to consider, starting tonight.

min_grade.name: Minimum grade
min_grade.description: Pink Milky Way nights only, include blue (short-window) nights, or any night regardless of the Milky Way.

min_score.name: Minimum score
min_score.description: Skip nights whose best site scores below this (0-100).

sort.name: Sort by
sort.description: Order the results by score, date or window length.

start.name: Start date
start.description: First night to consider. Defaults to tonight.

include_sites.name: Include every site
include_sites.description: Add the full site ranking for each night.

visible_targets.name: Visible targets
visible_targets.description: Lists the Messier objects, planets and custom targets that are up after dark at the Home Assistant location, with how long, how high and which direction. Returns the result as response data.

days.name: Nights
days.description: How many nights to look at, starting with the first.

kinds.name: Kinds
kinds.description: Only these kinds of object (all by default).

min_minutes.name: Minimum time up
min_minutes.description: Skip targets that are above the minimum altitude in the dark for less than this.
